exercises.description: Standing pushdown at the free-standing cable column, high pulley, straight bar. Strictest pushdown variant: the upper arm never moves.
execution: Set the pulley high and attach the straight bar.
Stand facing the column, feet shoulder-width, knees slightly flexed, back straight.
Grip the bar overhand and pin the elbows against the ribs.
Extend the elbows until the bar reaches the thighs.
Return under control until the elbows reach roughly 90 degrees.
cues: Only the forearms move
Ribs down, back straight
Upper arm stays vertical
common_errors: Leaning the torso forward to add bodyweight to the movement
Elbows drifting forward or flaring out
Shrugging the shoulders at lockout
rom_notes: Upper arm stays vertical throughout; the shoulder contributes nothing.

exercises.description: Seated pulldown at the lat machine with the long wide bar, thighs locked under the pads, bar pulled to the chest.
execution: Set the thigh pads so the legs are locked and the hips cannot rise.
Take the wide bar with an overhand grip wider than the shoulders.
Sit down with the torso close to upright and a slight backward lean.
Pull the bar down to the upper chest, driving the elbows down and back.
Return under control to full arm extension without letting the shoulders shrug up.
cues: Elbows down toward the floor, not back
Chest up to meet the bar
common_errors: Leaning far back and turning it into a row
Pulling with the hands rather than driving the elbows
Letting the shoulders ride up at the top
rom_notes: Bar to the upper chest; never behind the neck.

exercises.description: Same lat machine, close neutral grip using the short triangle handle. Narrower grip shifts emphasis toward the lower lats and loads the biceps more.
execution: Attach the triangle handle and set the thigh pads.
Take the handle with both palms facing each other.
Pull the handle down to the sternum, elbows tracking close to the ribs.
Return under control to full extension.
cues: Handle to the sternum
Elbows brush past the ribs
common_errors: Shortening the range at the bottom
Excessive backward lean

exercises.description: Seated machine press with a tall back pad, handles at shoulder height, pushed horizontally away from the chest.
execution: Set the seat so the handles sit at mid-chest height.
Sit with the whole back against the pad and the shoulders down.
Push the handles away from the chest until the arms are nearly straight.
Return under control until the elbows reach roughly 90 degrees.
cues: Shoulders stay down and back against the pad
Do not lock out hard
common_errors: Shoulders rolling forward at the end of the push
Elbows travelling behind the torso on the return
rom_notes: Do not let the elbow pass 90 degrees on the return; the shoulder should never be forced into extension behind the trunk.

exercises.description: Seated fly machine with forearm pads. Force is applied through the forearm against the pad, not through the hand on the grip.
execution: Set the seat so the pads meet the forearms at roughly shoulder height.
Sit back, place the forearms against the pads with the elbows bent, arms open wide.
Rest the hands on the grips without pushing through them.
Bring the arms together until the pads nearly touch in front of the chest.
Open under control back to the start.
cues: Push through the forearm, not the hand
Arms up 'like being arrested' at the start
common_errors: Gripping and pressing with the hands, turning it into a press
Opening so far that the shoulder is stretched at end range
rom_notes: Elbow angle stays fixed throughout; this is a fly, not a press.
cautions: Opening too wide at the start loads the front of the shoulder capsule.

exercises.description: Chest-supported machine row performed one arm at a time. Straddle seat, chest pad, handles forward. The free hand holds a fixed grip on the frame to brace.
execution: Set the seat so the chest pad meets the sternum and the handles are reachable at arm's length.
Straddle the seat, chest firmly against the pad.
Hold a fixed grip with the free hand, that arm staying horizontal and still.
Pull one handle back, driving the elbow low and past the ribs.
Return under control to full extension. Complete the weaker side first, then match its reps on the stronger side.
cues: Elbow toward the jeans pocket, not out wide
Chest never leaves the pad
common_errors: Chest lifting off the pad to add body english
Rotating the torso toward the working side
Flaring the elbow high, which changes the exercise
rom_notes: Low elbow path biases the lats; a deliberately high, flared elbow is a different exercise and should be a separate id.

exercises.description: Seated horizontal sled leg press, feet driving against a vertical platform.
execution: Set the seat so the knees are bent to roughly 90 degrees at the start.
Place the feet shoulder-width on the platform, mid-foot under the load.
Push until the legs are nearly straight, without locking the knees hard.
Return under control to the start depth, keeping the lower back against the seat.
cues: Knees track over the toes
Lower back stays flat against the seat
common_errors: Letting the pelvis tuck at the bottom, rounding the lower back
Locking the knees at the top
rom_notes: Stop the return before the pelvis lifts off the seat.
cautions: Flat, fully pronated feet: check that the knees track over the feet through the whole range and do not fall inward near the bottom. See health.md, 'Feet'.

exercises.description: Seated knee extension. Hips locked by a lap pad, roller across the front of the shins, legs pushed up against resistance pushing down.
execution: Set the backrest so there are two fingers of space between the back of the knee and the seat edge.
Set the roller across the front of the lower shin, above the ankle.
Lock the lap pad so the hips cannot rise.
Extend the knees until the legs are straight.
Lower under control without letting the weight stack touch down.
cues: Two fingers of gap at the knee
Pause briefly at the top
common_errors: Sliding forward in the seat so the knee axis no longer matches the machine's pivot
Using the hands on the grips to pull the torso and add momentum
rom_notes: Knee joint must align with the machine's rotation axis.

exercises.description: Prone back extension on a vertical Roman chair. Thighs on the pad, heels hooked under the rear rollers, torso lowered to horizontal and raised back in line.
execution: Set the pad just below the hip crease and hook the heels under the rollers.
Cross the arms over the chest.
Lower the torso until the body is horizontal.
Raise until the body is straight, without arching beyond a straight line.
cues: Stop at straight, do not hyperextend
Arms crossed like a mummy
Do not stand up straight away - pause on the handles first
common_errors: Arching hard past neutral at the top
Bouncing out of the bottom
rom_notes: Top position is a straight line, not an arch.

Low blood pressure: after the set, hold the handles and come up in stages, pausing a couple of seconds before standing fully upright. Twenty-plus reps with the head below the heart followed by standing is a classic setup for a pressure drop.
cautions: See health.md, 'Circulation'. The end-of-set pause is a standing instruction, not an optional precaution.

exercises.description: Full sit-up on a decline abdominal bench with the ankles hooked under rollers, performed through the complete range up to the rollers.
execution: Set the bench one notch short of maximum incline.
Hook the ankles under the rollers and lie back.
Curl up through the full range until the face is near the rollers.
Lower under control to the start.
cues: Lead with the ribs, not the neck
Pause sitting before standing off the bench
common_errors: Pulling on the head or neck
Dropping back down without control
rom_notes: Full range makes this substantially a hip flexor exercise, not a pure abdominal one.
Head-below-heart position. Same standing rule as the Roman chair: sit up, pause, then stand.
cautions: High-volume loaded spinal flexion. Keep the volume moderate where spinal considerations apply.
Low blood pressure: see health.md, 'Circulation'.

exercises.description: Split-stance lunge holding a dumbbell in each hand at the sides. Each leg is loaded independently; the dumbbells hang rather than compressing the spine from above.
execution: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand at the sides.
Step forward into a split stance and lower until the rear knee is near the floor.
Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
Alternate legs, or complete all reps on one leg before switching.
cues: Torso upright
Front knee tracks over the foot
Weight through the whole foot; do not let the knee drift inward
common_errors: Leaning the torso over the front thigh
Steps too short, putting the knee far ahead of the foot
cautions: Learn the pattern with bodyweight before adding dumbbells.
Flat, fully pronated feet: watch that the front knee tracks over the foot rather than collapsing inward as the arch flattens under load. See health.md, 'Feet'.

exercises.description: Standing lateral raise performed one arm at a time, the free hand bracing on a fixed upright. Builds the side delt without the load ever passing overhead.
execution: Hold a light dumbbell in one hand, the other hand braced on a rack upright.
With a slight bend in the elbow, raise the arm out to the side.
Stop at shoulder height, no higher.
Lower under control. Complete the weaker side first and match its reps on the stronger side.
cues: Stop level with the shoulder
Lead with the elbow, not the hand
common_errors: Raising above shoulder height
Swinging the torso to launch the weight
Shrugging the trapezius to finish the rep
rom_notes: Never above shoulder height - this is what keeps the movement non-overhead.
cautions: Stopping level with the shoulder is what keeps this movement non-overhead, which is a firm constraint here. See health.md, 'Shoulder'.

Home pair is 3 kg, at which 20 reps are comfortable on all but the last set - below the useful training range. Use gym dumbbells for working sets; the home pair is for keeping the pattern warm, not for progression.

exercises.description: Standing or seated dumbbell curl, one arm at a time. The catalogue's only direct elbow-flexion exercise. Verified: performed at home with a modular dumbbell.
execution: Stand or sit with a dumbbell in one hand, arm hanging at the side, back straight.
Keep the elbow pinned against the ribs and the palm supinated, so the handle stays level through the movement.
Curl the weight up to the chest, moving only the forearm.
Lower under control to full extension.
Complete the weaker side first and match its reps on the stronger side.
cues: Elbow stays pinned to the ribs
Only the forearm moves
Full extension at the bottom
common_errors: Swinging the elbow forward at the top
Using the torso to start the rep

Bracing by reaching the free arm behind the back - it works, but parks that shoulder in extension and internal rotation for the whole set. Sitting on a chair with a back achieves the same anti-swing effect with nothing held behind the body.
rom_notes: Arm straight at the bottom; the shortened range is where most of the load is lost.
cautions: Home modular dumbbell load ladder is 1 / 3 / 5 / 7 / 9 kg only (1 kg handle, 2x2 kg and 4x1 kg discs loaded symmetrically). Currently at 7 kg, so ONE step remains and 7->9 kg is a 28% jump. A set of 0.5 kg discs would halve the increment to 1 kg and is the cheapest possible fix.
Gym dumbbells offer finer increments and no ceiling - prefer them once past 9 kg.

exercises.description: Calf raise performed on the horizontal leg press by placing the balls of the feet at the bottom edge of the platform. Uses a machine already in the program, so it adds no setup time.
execution: Sit in the leg press with the balls of the feet on the lower edge of the platform, heels off.
Straighten the legs but keep a soft knee.
Push the platform away by plantarflexing the ankles.
Let the heels travel back toward the shins under control for a full stretch.
cues: Full stretch at the bottom, full push at the top
Do not bend the knees to help
common_errors: Bouncing through a very short range
Bending the knees to turn it into a press
rom_notes: Range matters more than load here.
cautions: Flat, fully pronated feet: keep the load through the ball of the foot behind the first and fifth toes rather than rolling to the inside edge. See health.md, 'Feet'.

exercises.description: Isometric side hold on the forearm. Trains the trunk to resist being bent sideways - the frontal plane, where a lateral spinal curve lives.
execution: Lie on one side, forearm on the floor, elbow under the shoulder.
Stack the feet and lift the hips so the body forms a straight line.
Hold, breathing normally.
Repeat on the other side. Record both sides; a large difference is information worth keeping.
cues: Hips high, body in one line
Do not let the top shoulder roll forward
common_errors: Hips sagging toward the floor
Rotating toward the floor to make the hold easier

exercises.description: Standing anti-rotation press at a cable column set to chest height. The cable tries to twist the torso; the job is to refuse.
execution: Set the pulley to chest height and stand side-on, feet shoulder-width.
Hold the handle with both hands at the sternum.
Press the hands straight out in front of the chest, resisting the pull toward the column.
Hold briefly, return to the chest. Repeat facing the other way.
cues: Do not let the torso rotate at all
Hips and shoulders stay square
common_errors: Letting the torso turn toward the column
Using a weight so heavy that rotation is unavoidable
rom_notes: This is an anti-rotation exercise: the spine should not rotate under load.

exercises.description: Lying face down, raising one arm and the opposite leg. Trains the erectors and glutes one side at a time while the trunk resists rotating. Needs no equipment and works at home.
execution: Lie face down, arms extended overhead, gaze down at the floor.
Raise one arm and the opposite leg a few centimetres off the floor.
Hold for about two seconds. The resting hand may stay in contact with the floor.
Lower and repeat on the other side.
cues: Keep looking at the floor, do not lift the head
Raise slowly, no swinging
common_errors: Craning the neck to look forward
Lifting so high that the lower back arches hard
rom_notes: A few centimetres is enough; height is not the point.

exercises.description: Seated machine press driving handles overhead. Retained in the library as a record of a movement that was tried and dropped - see the log for the reason.
execution: Set the seat so the handles start at shoulder height.
Press the handles upward until the arms are nearly straight.
Lower under control to the start.
cautions: Caused a week of LOST OVERHEAD RANGE at roughly 15-20 kg - difficulty raising the arm enough to dress. Felt fine during the session; the problem appeared afterwards.
This was not delayed-onset muscle soreness: the load was trivial and DOMS does not remove range of motion for a week. See health.md, 'Shoulder'.
The same shoulder pops painlessly when raising a load overhead, and the movement is felt to be not smooth.
Fixed bilateral overhead path; the stronger side compensates and the asymmetry is loaded rather than trained.
Do not reintroduce. This is a firm constraint, not a preference to revisit once stronger. Lateral raises cover the side delt without going overhead.

exercises.description: Seated cable row. Horizontal pad, two angled foot platforms facing the user, cable emerging at seated chest height. Unsupported torso, so the trunk works isometrically throughout - a bigger movement than the lat pulldown and rated as markedly harder.
execution: Sit on the pad and plant both feet on the angled platforms, knees slightly bent.
Take the handle with a neutral spine - bend at the hips with the knees bent, or scoot forward, rather than rounding over to reach it.
Sit up with the torso close to vertical, a slight backward lean only.
Pull the handle to the lower chest, driving the elbows back past the ribs and letting the shoulder blades come together.
Return under control to full arm extension without letting the torso get pulled forward into flexion.
cues: Chest tall, lean back only slightly
Drive the elbows back, squeeze the shoulder blades
Do not let the cable pull you into a round back on the return
common_errors: Rocking the torso back and forth, which turns a back exercise into a lumbar one
Rounding forward on the return under load
Reaching for the handle from a rounded-over position at the start
rom_notes: Torso stays within roughly 10-15 degrees of vertical throughout. The range comes from the arms and shoulder blades, not from the spine.
cautions: Taking the handle is the most lumbar-loading instant in the whole routine: reaching forward for a loaded stack with a rounded back. Set up with bent knees and a neutral spine. See health.md.
Not comparable to the lat pulldown by load. 45 kg here and 55 kg there are different machines and different movements.

exercises.description: Prone isometric hold on the forearms, body in a straight line. Anti-extension trunk work. Performed at home, currently 60-80 seconds.
execution: Forearms on the floor, elbows under the shoulders, feet together.
Lift the hips so head, hips and heels form one line.
Brace and breathe normally for the hold.
cues: One straight line, hips neither sagging nor piked
Squeeze the glutes
common_errors: Hips sagging
Holding the breath
Adding time instead of adding difficulty
rom_notes: Past roughly 45-60 seconds this becomes an endurance test rather than a strength stimulus. Progress by making it harder - lifting one foot or reaching one arm forward, which also adds an anti-rotation demand - not by holding longer.

exercises.description: Standard floor push-up. Self-reported as difficult despite a well-trained machine chest press - see cautions, the limiter is probably trunk stability rather than pressing strength.
execution: Hands slightly wider than the shoulders, body in one straight line from head to heels.
Lower with the elbows at roughly 45 degrees to the torso, not flared wide.
Press back up without letting the hips sag or pike.
Elevate the hands on a bench or countertop to scale; lower the surface over months to progress.
cues: It is a plank that presses - hold the line first
Elbows at 45 degrees, not out wide
common_errors: Hips sagging or piking
Elbows flaring to 90 degrees
Chasing depth at the bottom
rom_notes: Do NOT chase chest-to-floor depth. The bottom position is where a restricted shoulder is least protected - see health.md.
cautions: A push-up is a plank that presses. Given a well-trained chest press and a very mobile trunk, the likely limiter is holding a rigid line, not pressing strength - passive range far exceeds active control. TEST: elevate the hands. If it suddenly feels easy, the limiter was trunk stability; if still hard, it is pressing strength.
Rigidly bilateral in the same way a machine is: hands fixed, one path, and the stronger side can take more of the load unnoticed. Bodyweight does not 'self-balance'.

exercises.description: Unloaded squat. At a 95-100 kg leg press this is a movement-quality drill rather than a training stimulus - useful for knee tracking, not for building anything.
execution: Feet shoulder-width, weight through the whole foot.
Sit down and back, keeping the knees tracking over the feet.
Descend only as far as the position can be actively controlled.
Drive up through the heels.
cues: Knees track over the feet, do not let them fall inward
Stop where you still have control
common_errors: Knees collapsing inward as the arches flatten
Sinking to the bottom and resting on passive structures
rom_notes: Do not chase depth. With very mobile hips the bottom of a deep squat is passive end range, where the musculature has no authority. See health.md.
cautions: Flat, fully pronated feet: this is the main reason to do it at all - watch knee tracking. See health.md, 'Feet'.

exercises.description: Seated machine knee flexion. CONFIRMED on site 2026-09-19: exists, seated type, 5 kg stack increments. The only dedicated hamstring exercise available.
execution: Set the back pad so the knee joint lines up with the machine's pivot.
Place the roller against the back of the lower calf, above the Achilles.
Lock the lap pad so the hips cannot lift.
Flex the knees through the full available range.
Return under control without letting the stack rest between reps.
cues: Hips stay pinned under the pad
Control the return, do not let it snap back
common_errors: Lifting the hips to gain range
Range collapsing at the end of the set
rom_notes: Do not force the stretched position at the top of the return - end range is where an untrained hamstring is least protected. See health.md.
cautions: Hamstrings have never been trained directly. Start well below what feels right; first-exposure soreness here is pronounced and lasts days.

exercises.description: Seated calf raise - straddled seat with a pad across the thighs. CONFIRMED on site 2026-09-19. The bent knee shortens the gastrocnemius, which shifts the work onto the SOLEUS - the one calf muscle a leg-press calf raise does not reach.
execution: Sit with the balls of the feet on the platform and the pad across the lower thighs.
Let the heels drop for a full stretch.
Press up onto the balls of the feet through the full range.
Lower under control.
cues: Full range beats heavy load here
Pause briefly at the top
common_errors: Short bouncing reps
Loading so heavily the range collapses
cautions: Complements rather than duplicates leg-press calf raises: bent knee targets soleus, straight knee targets gastrocnemius.

exercises.description: Seated hip abduction - pads outside the knees, legs driven apart. CONFIRMED on site 2026-09-19 (the 'no' half of the yes/no pair). The only direct gluteus medius work available.
execution: Sit with the pads against the outside of the knees.
Drive the knees apart through the available range.
Return under control without letting the stack rest.
cues: Sit tall, do not lean back to gain leverage
Control the return
common_errors: Rocking the torso to move the weight
Very short jerky range
rom_notes: Do not push into end range. Hip mobility is already abundant - see health.md.

exercises.description: Standing single-leg hip extension against a pad. CONFIRMED on site 2026-09-19, never used. Unilateral by construction, which suits the asymmetry constraints well.
execution: Stand facing the frame, holding the handles, torso upright.
Place one leg against the pad.
Drive the leg back and down by extending the hip, without arching the lower back.
Return under control. Weaker side first, stronger side matches its reps.
cues: Movement comes from the hip, not from arching the back
Torso stays still
common_errors: Arching the lumbar spine to gain range
Leaning the torso forward as the leg goes back
rom_notes: Stop when the hip stops moving - any further range is the lower back, not the glute.

exercises.description: Machine hip thrust. CONFIRMED on site 2026-09-19: feet planted on a platform with knees at roughly 90 degrees, upper back flat on the cushion, pelvis driven up against a rolling pad. Supine and supported, no spinal compression, nothing overhead - fits the constraints in health.md unusually well.
execution: Sit with the upper back against the cushion and the roller pad across the hips.
Plant the feet on the platform, knees at about 90 degrees at the top.
Drive the hips up until the torso and thighs form a line.
Lower under control without letting the weight rest at the bottom.
cues: Drive through the heels
Finish with the glutes, not by arching the back
Ribs down
common_errors: Hyperextending the lower back at the top instead of finishing with the glutes
Feet too close, turning it into a quad exercise
rom_notes: The top position is a straight line, not an arch.
cautions: Plate-loaded and somewhat clunky to set up. Widely assumed to be a machine for women; that is gym folklore, not a property of the equipment.

exercises.description: Rope face pull at a cable column set to roughly head height. Replaces the reverse pec deck, which does not exist at this gym - the pec deck does not reverse. Better suited anyway: constant tension, free path, and easily done one arm at a time.
execution: Set the pulley at about head height and attach a rope handle.
Stand with a staggered stance, arms extended forward.
Pull the rope toward the face, driving the elbows high and outward.
Finish with the hands beside the ears and the shoulder blades together.
Return under control.
cues: Elbows high and wide
Pull the rope apart as it arrives
Shoulders down, do not shrug
common_errors: Elbows dropping, turning it into a row
Shrugging the traps to finish
Leaning back to move a heavier stack
rom_notes: Stop where the shoulder blades stop moving; do not force the end position.
cautions: Can be done single-arm, which is preferred here. Keep the load light enough that the elbows stay high - dropping them changes the exercise.
